items.why: The report gives raw shifts of "E' 383.33 -> 385.83 (+2.51) and A1' 404.88 -> 407.31 (+2.43), i.e. the same rigid shift," and an unchanged separation of "21.56 vs 21.47 cm-1".
It states the "Si substrate line moved by the same amount (519.98 to 522.47 cm-1), so the spectrometer calibration drifted between days".
After Si correction, "E'-like 384.05 +/- 0.01 vs 384.07 +/- 0.02... both shifts consistent with zero", and "The separation of 21.5 cm-1 points to bilayer (2L)" on both days.

It says "Nothing supports the colleague's adsorbate doping or strain hypothesis", that the widths are unchanged so there is "no broadening signature of doping", and that "Doping (A1' led) and strain (E' led, with splitting) would not move both modes together".
It asks: "Why did the Si reference line move by 2.5 cm-1 between days (grating move, recalibration, different spectral window)?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain and doping: "strain_sign: none" and "doping_type: none (no change between days)".
The report assigns 2L on both days ("Same result on both days") and says "defect_level: none detected".
